html:
The Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, or Bingtuan, is a state company and paramilitary body that farms, builds and governs large parts of Xinjiang in northwest China. It was set up in 1954 on the orders of Mao Zedong.

Its first members were demobilised soldiers who had taken Xinjiang for the new People's Republic. It follows an old Chinese model, the tuntian, in which soldiers farmed the frontier and held it at the same time. Over the decades it brought in millions of Han Chinese settlers, dug canals, opened farms in the desert and built whole cities such as Shihezi, which it runs itself.

The Corps has its own courts, police and schools, and is a major grower of cotton. It changed the population of northern Xinjiang, where the Uyghurs and Kazakhs had been the majority. The United States put sanctions on it in 2020, over its part in the campaign that includes the Xinjiang internment camps.
